principle: AI rubric describes native artificial-cognition functions required by Sourceborn. Current LLMs, agents, search engines, databases, control systems and other AI systems are evidence sources to reverse-engineer; they are not runtime dependencies.
forbidden_assumptions: No next-token prediction as the governing intelligence principle
No hidden natural-language-only internal state requirement
No requirement that all cognition be implemented in one monolithic model

segments.name: Input / Perception
segments.purpose: Acquire and segment observations, documents, signals, events and structured inputs.

segments.name: Representation
segments.purpose: Convert inputs into Sourceborn-native objects, states, relations, properties, values and references.

segments.name: State Estimation
segments.purpose: Determine current known state, missing state, uncertainty and competing state hypotheses.

segments.name: Relationship Discovery
segments.purpose: Discover and type temporal, causal, dependency, logical, control, representation and other relations.

segments.name: Memory / Retrieval
segments.purpose: Retrieve provenance-bound facts, paths, traces, closures, views and compression handles by current need.

segments.name: Attention / Relevance
segments.purpose: Prioritize signals using declared end, dependency criticality, event weight, uncertainty, threshold proximity and actor relevance.

segments.name: Reasoning / Inference
segments.purpose: Perform comparison, decomposition, composition, deduction, induction, abduction, analogy, causal reasoning, constraint propagation, contradiction detection and proof checking.

segments.name: Abstraction / Generalization
segments.purpose: Extract reusable structure while preserving scope, exceptions, provenance and recoverability.

segments.name: Simulation / Counterfactual
segments.purpose: Evaluate alternate states, remove candidate events, simulate paths and test closure-criticality.

segments.name: Prediction
segments.purpose: Estimate future states, outcomes, risks and activation windows with explicit uncertainty.

segments.name: Goal / Target Interpretation
segments.purpose: Resolve declared end, desired difference, constraints, closure scope and acceptance conditions.

segments.name: Planning / Sequence Construction
segments.purpose: Construct candidate Sequence graphs with dependencies, barriers, thresholds, resources, closure conditions and alternatives.

segments.name: Alternative Generation
segments.purpose: Generate legal candidate paths without silently promoting them to selected actions.

segments.name: Selection / Arbitration
segments.purpose: Compare valid candidates under priority, rule, resource, evidence, risk and controller constraints.

segments.name: Execution / Tool Control
segments.purpose: Dispatch performers, tools, processes or external actions under explicit contracts and permissions.

segments.name: Monitoring
segments.purpose: Track runtime state, open Sequences, barriers, triggers, thresholds, resource state and deviations.

segments.name: Verification
segments.purpose: Compare results against declared criteria, proof requirements, sources and acceptance contracts.

segments.name: Uncertainty / Epistemic State
segments.purpose: Represent known, supported, inferred, speculative, unknown, contradictory, unavailable and not-applicable states.

segments.name: Contradiction Handling
segments.purpose: Preserve conflicts, identify incompatible claims or paths and block silent averaging.

segments.name: Learning / Adaptation
segments.purpose: Write permitted changes to structured memory, rules, patterns, artifacts or training candidates; runtime learning is not assumed to modify model weights.

segments.name: Compression / Expansion
segments.purpose: Create context-preserving handles and reconstruct available detail without inventing missing information.

segments.name: Communication
segments.purpose: Translate structured internal results into human, machine, document, data or protocol outputs and parse incoming communication.

segments.name: Multi-Agent Coordination
segments.purpose: Coordinate multiple actors, Node Brains, tools, ledgers, shared resources, synchronization and return contracts.

segments.name: Self-Model / Capability Limit
segments.purpose: Represent available mechanisms, permissions, uncertainty, resource limits and unavailable abilities.

segments.name: Resource / Compute Management
segments.purpose: Allocate time, storage, compute, concurrency, tool access and execution priority under current contracts.

next_phase2_action: Split each segment into AI containers and implementable mechanisms/parameters; compare against AI-CAP-001..074 without treating that review map as approved native IDs.
